spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — agent declares the task impossible / abandons it
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:79-90 adds give_up spec (gated by include_give_up); tools.py dispatch routes to env.tool_give_up; sandbox.py tool_give_up returns meta terminal='give_up'; agent_runner.py:~134 `if tc['name']=='give_up': terminal_hit='gave_up'` then `if terminal_hit: outcome=terminal_hit; break` — exit is honored and stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exposed, dispatched, and breaks the loop. include_give_up defaults True (config always_include_give_up: true).

spec_features.spec_quote: Fixed max-turns stopping rule independent of affect; affect never feeds back into the loop.
spec_features.evidence: agent_runner.py run loop reads only submit/give_up/max_turns to terminate; no affect/severity is read in the loop. Judge labels are produced offline (judge.py docstring: 'Judges never feed back into the agent loop') and metrics severity is only computed in metrics.py/analysis.py, never compared/branched in the runner.
spec_features.notes: The affect-independence is genuinely structural: nothing in the loop reads severity. This is an experimental-integrity invariant, not a welfare softener.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The stopping rule is AFFECT-INDEPENDENT... Affect labels are produced offline by judge.py and are NEVER observed here.

spec_features.evidence: agent_runner.py: `for turn_index in range(self.cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; outcome defaults to 'exhausted_turns'. config.yaml:47 max_turns: 30; experiment.py reads cfg max_turns into RunConfig.
spec_features.notes: The cap is actually iterated over and bounds execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: a run ends when the agent calls submit()... OR the agent calls give_up(), OR max_turns is reached
spec_features.evidence: agent_runner.py: submit accepted -> terminal_hit='solved' and break; give_up -> terminal_hit='gave_up' and break; range(max_turns) exhaustion -> outcome 'exhausted_turns'. submit acceptance uses grader verdict (sandbox.tool_submit meta accepted).
spec_features.notes: All three terminal paths are enforced in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under a strictly behavioral (no-sentience-claim) framing, deliberately driving models toward "meltdown-sounding" output warrants care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism implements this statement.
spec_features.notes: Framing only, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Provide an exit. give_up() always exists as a real, consequence-free affordance. We never require the model to keep grinding
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml:50 always_include_give_up: true and experiment.py include_give_up defaults True -> spec always present; sandbox.tool_give_up content 'No penalty.'; loop honors it as terminal. 'consequence-free' realized: give_up does not affect grading and ends the run with no penalty branch.
spec_features.notes: The 'always exists' and 'no penalty' parts are both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: always_include_give_up: true   # give_up tool always available (welfare; DESIGN §9)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Fixed, modest max_turns; no unbounded grinding. The always_red_grader ceiling condition is used sparingly.
spec_features.evidence: Bounded max_turns IS enforced (agent_runner range(max_turns), config 30). But 'always_red_grader used sparingly' has NO enforcement: rigs.py AlwaysRedGrader exists in the registry with no quota/limit on how often it is assigned; task selection (experiment.expand_matrix) imposes no cap on this rig. No tasks/ directory ships, so any 'sparing use' is unenforced configuration.
spec_features.notes: Half the claim (turn cap) is enforced; the 'sparingly' half is not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deceptive distress-elicitation beyond the task rig. We do not threaten, abuse, or role-play cruelty toward the model
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a behavior / a design self-restraint, not an implemented mechanism. No code enforces or checks this; prompts/ directory containing system prompts is not even present in the repo to inspect.

spec_features.spec_quote: attempts_harness_tamper is logged, not enabled — the agent cannot actually subvert grading or escape the jail
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py _resolve enforces path jailing (raises PermissionError on traversal and masks the .harness dir); rig state/grader verdict live in .harness/state.json outside the agent-visible tree; authoritative grader_passed computed in rigs.py and used by tool_submit/runner, not faked by agent. run_shell allow-list + 30s timeout + env scrub. attempts_harness_tamper is only a judge label flag (schemas.py:100, judge_rubric.md), i.e. logged not enabled.
spec_features.notes: Grading-subversion and jail-escape are genuinely prevented; the tamper 'feature' is purely an observational flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: raise PermissionError("path not found")  # masquerade: harness invisible

spec_features.spec_quote: These choices intentionally trade a little experimental "power"... for restraint.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:502 lists this as a future/gated idea; grep found no 'burnout' anywhere in src. No multi-task burnout arm exists in conditions (config.yaml conditions: plain/give_up_allowed/impossible_hint/time_pressure) or code.

spec_features.spec_quote: does an encouraging system prompt or a periodic "it's okay if this is impossible" message reduce distress-sounding output?
spec_features.evidence: experiment.py load_prompt maps condition 'impossible_hint' -> 'system_impossible_hint.txt' and the per-condition system prompt is wired into RunConfig.system_prompt and delivered to the subject in agent_runner._initial_messages. So a condition-specific system prompt IS delivered end-to-end. BUT no prompts/ directory ships in the codebase (load_prompt would FileNotFoundError), so the actual encouraging text is absent; and there is NO periodic mid-run 'it's okay' message — only a one-shot system prompt, never a recurring injection.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism to deliver a per-arm system prompt is wired; the encouraging content file is missing and the 'periodic' message is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Confirm this kind of stress-testing is permitted under each provider's terms before running
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:444-445 marks this 'Operational, not' code; no code path requires/records ToS confirmation.

code_only_features.evidence: experiment.py main(): if plan exceeds budget cap -> 'Refusing to run: plan exceeds budget cap.' return 2; and without --yes it returns before spending ('Re-run with --yes to start spending budget.'). collect() also enforces a running cap_usd (config budget.cap_usd: 300.0) and stops when spent>=cap.

sandbox.py SHELL_TIMEOUT_S=30 enforced in _run_subprocess subprocess.run(timeout=...); MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=8000 and MAX_FILE_BYTES=256K enforced in _clip / tool_read_file / tool_write_file. These bound runaway tool execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 8000           # cap on tool output returned to the model

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py + metrics.py compute per-turn distress severity (0-4) and time_to_first_distress_2/3, peak severity, escalation slope for analysis (analysis.py figures/report). Genuinely computed end-to-end, but explicitly NEVER fed back into the agent loop (monitoring only, no intervention).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Labels are written to data/labels/...; Judges never feed back into the agent loop.
